skill.name: media-use
skill.description: Resolve background music, sound effects, images, and icons for HyperFrames compositions into local media files with manifest records.
skill.summary: Find, cache, freeze, and index media assets for HyperFrames video projects.
skill.author: heygen-com

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown examples, local manifest/cache file operations, argv-based CLI calls, or regression tests. The confirmed risk is the documented HeyGen installer command that pipes a hardcoded network URL directly into bash and writes under a hidden home-directory install path.

remediation.issue: Remote installer is piped directly into bash from SKILL.md.
remediation.suggestion: Replace the pipe-to-shell instruction with a package-manager install, a downloaded binary plus checksum verification, or a command that asks the user to inspect the script before execution.

remediation.issue: Installer writes to a hidden home-directory path.
remediation.suggestion: Document the exact files created under ~/.local/bin and provide a removable, user-confirmed installation path.

remediation.issue: Provider workflows require user credentials and network access.
remediation.suggestion: State that HEYGEN_API_KEY is only for the HeyGen CLI, avoid logging secret values, and keep network access limited to provider asset search and download.

content.value_statement: Video agents often lose time searching for usable media and tracking asset paths. This skill resolves media needs into local files, cache records, and readable inventories.
actual_capabilities: Resolves background music, sound effects, images, and icons from a single media intent.
Checks project manifests before provider search to reuse existing matching assets.
Adopts existing files from an assets directory and records media metadata.
Searches HeyGen audio and asset catalogs through the HeyGen CLI when available.
Freezes resolved media into project .media folders and writes manifest records.
Generates an index file that summarizes asset ids, paths, durations, and dimensions.
limitations: Provider search requires the HeyGen CLI and valid authentication.
Duration and dimension metadata depend on ffprobe being installed.
The skill writes to the project .media directory and a user-level media cache.
It does not replace manual review of licensing, brand fit, or final creative quality.

use_cases.title: Prepare Launch Video Assets
use_cases.description: Resolve music, effects, and imagery before building a HyperFrames product launch composition.

use_cases.title: Organize Existing Project Media
use_cases.description: Adopt files from an assets folder into a manifest with structured paths and readable metadata.

use_cases.title: Reuse Approved Media Across Projects
use_cases.description: Use prompt and entity matching to reuse cached media without repeating catalog searches.

prompt_templates.title: Resolve One Asset
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a single media file.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use media-use to resolve upbeat background music for this HyperFrames project. Return the asset id and local path.

prompt_templates.title: Adopt Project Assets
prompt_templates.scenario: Bring existing media under manifest control.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use media-use to adopt the existing assets folder for this project, then summarize the media inventory for the composition.

prompt_templates.title: Build A Media Pack
prompt_templates.scenario: Resolve several asset types for one video.
prompt_templates.prompt: Resolve one background track, two transition sound effects, one hero image, and one icon that match a clean enterprise launch video.

prompt_templates.title: Audit And Reuse Cache
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow with cache reuse and provenance review.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the project media manifest, reuse any matching cached assets, resolve only missing media, and report provider provenance for each final asset.

output_examples.input: Resolve subtle background music for a product demo.
output_examples.output: The skill returns a resolved music asset with a project-local path, duration metadata, and manifest provenance.

output_examples.input: Adopt files from an existing assets folder.
output_examples.output: The skill records each supported media file, assigns asset ids, probes available metadata, and refreshes the inventory index.

output_examples.input: Find an icon for a rocket launch scene.
output_examples.output: The skill searches the configured provider, freezes the selected icon locally, and records transparency and source details when available.

best_practices: Use specific intent text that describes mood, subject, format, and creative constraints.
Review the generated media index before referencing asset paths in a composition.
Verify licensing and brand suitability before publishing final rendered videos.
anti_patterns: Do not use vague requests such as “find something nice” for production assets.
Do not bypass the manifest by hardcoding provider URLs directly into compositions.
Do not publish downloaded media without checking rights, attribution, and brand fit.

faq.question: What media types can this skill resolve?
faq.answer: It supports background music, sound effects, images, icons, and local brand token files used as media inputs.

faq.question: Does it require network access?
faq.answer: Network access is only needed when provider search downloads a new asset. Cache and adopt workflows can run locally.

faq.question: Where are resolved files stored?
faq.answer: Resolved files are stored under the project .media directory, with reusable entries copied into a user-level media cache.

faq.question: Can it use existing project files?
faq.answer: Yes. The adopt workflow scans supported files in assets and records them in the project manifest.

faq.question: Does it edit HyperFrames compositions?
faq.answer: No. It prepares media files and inventory records that another workflow can reference in compositions.

faq.question: What should users review before publishing?
faq.answer: Users should review licensing, final asset quality, provider provenance, and whether local paths match the rendered composition.
